Council ruled 2027-08-28 and 2028-08-16; the engine gives 08-29 and 08-17, and Drik Panchang (Tier 5, commercial -- QA signal only) agrees with the ENGINE for 2028. Our 2026 date (09-08) is council-confirmed and reproduces, so only these two years are withheld. There is no Paryushana evaluator, so this is NOT resolved by USE_CONDITION_EVALUATOR -- an earlier claim of mine that was wrong. May need a Jain-profile or externally-curated treatment. DEEPER DIAGNOSIS 2026-08-18 (still not resolved, but now a precise, falsifiable finding instead of 'no convention found'): sampled the raw tithi (elongation-based, bypassing all handlers) at sunrise/madhyahna/aparahna/sunset for both ruled dates and their neighbours. Target is absolute tithi index 27 (krishna dwadashi). For 2027: tithi 27 does NOT touch 08-28's sunrise (still 26) but DOES touch 08-28's madhyahna/aparahna/sunset (begins between sunrise and madhyahna that day) -- a madhyahna-vyapini-style convention (same family as D34's four fixed rules) would land exactly on the council's 08-28 ruling. For 2028: tithi 27 does NOT touch 08-16 at ANY sampled point of the day -- sunrise, madhyahna, aparahna, and sunset are all still tithi 26 throughout 08-16; tithi 27 only begins close to 08-17's own sunrise. No reference-time convention this engine knows how to express reproduces the 08-16 ruling. Since the same festival cannot correctly follow two different reference-time rules in different years, this rules out a simple fixed-convention fix for BOTH years at once. Two live hypotheses, neither confirmed: (a) 2028's council ruling is itself the outlier and needs an independent re-check against a primary Jain source, structurally the same situation karva-chauth 2028 turned out to be (D40) -- Drik Panchang already agrees with the engine's 08-17 for 2028, which is corroborating, not sourcing, evidence; or (b) Paryushana's real governing rule isn't 'tithi 27 at some fixed time of day' at all -- Jain paksha/tithi reckoning has genuine, documented sect-level calendar disputes (distinct from the Vedic madhyahna/nishitha family), and may need a dedicated Jain-calendar source, not an extension of this engine's existing reference-time mechanism. Needs a human with access to a primary Jain panchang (e.g. a Shvetambara Murtipujak source) to adjudicate -- engineering cannot pick between (a) and (b) from computation alone. PARKED 2026-08-18 (founder decision): no Tier 1-4 Jain calendar authority has ever been identified in this project (see docs/sources/candidate-sources-sikh-buddhist-jain.md) -- both hypotheses above require one before further work is useful. Jain and Buddhist calendar sourcing deprioritized as a body of work, to be picked up together later. 2026 (09-08) stays published; 2027/2028 stay withheld. No further engineering action until a primary Jain source is available.
